hints: The number of faulty components F follows B(200, 0.15).
Find the parameters for the approximating normal distribution: mean mu = 200 * 0.15 = 30 and variance sigma^2 = 30 * 0.85 = 25.5.
Apply the continuity correction to F > 40 (discrete F >= 41): P(F_cont > 40.5).
walkthrough:
Step 1: Set up the binomial distribution:
- Sample size $n = 200$
- Probability of a component being faulty $p = 0.15$
- Probability of not being faulty $q = 1 - 0.15 = 0.85$
- Distribution: $F \sim \mathrm{B}(200, 0.15)$.

Step 2: Check conditions and compute normal parameters:
- $n p = 200 \times 0.15 = 30 > 5$
- $n q = 200 \times 0.85 = 170 > 5$
Both conditions are met, so a normal approximation is appropriate.
$$\mu = n p = 30$$
$$\sigma^2 = n p q = 30 \times 0.85 = 25.5$$
$$\sigma = \sqrt{25.5} \approx 5.049752$$

Step 3: Apply the continuity correction:
We need the probability that 'more than 40' components are faulty.
For discrete integers, this means $F \ge 41$.
On the continuous normal scale, the discrete integer 41 begins at its lower boundary $40.5$:
$$\mathrm{P}(F > 40) = \mathrm{P}(F \ge 41) \approx \mathrm{P}(F_{\text{normal}} > 40.5)$$

Step 5: Compute the upper-tail probability:
$$\mathrm{P}(Z > 2.079) = 1 - \Phi(2.079)$$
From the normal distribution table:
$$\Phi(2.07) = 0.9808$$
Difference for $9$: $+0.0004$
$$\Phi(2.079) = 0.9812$$
$$\mathrm{P}(Z > 2.079) = 1 - 0.9812 = 0.0188$$
